uncited: It builds on [Splatting and Point-based Rendering](4975-splatting-and-point-based-rendering.md) and differs from siblings such as [Ray-Box Intersection via Quad Rasterization](2253-ray-box-intersection-via-quad-rasterization.md), [Sparse Voxel Octree Rendering via Square Splats](2993-sparse-voxel-octree-rendering-via-square-splats.md), [Voxel Point Sprite Rendering](4307-voxel-point-sprite-rendering.md), and [Differentiable Point-Based Radiance Fields](7366-differentiable-point-based-radiance-fields.md) by relying on explicit voxel culling and a custom segment-based storage layout rather than hierarchical traversal or differentiable field representations.
Initialize a **Buffer Plane** (depth buffer) with dimensions equal to the screen plane ($W \times H$).
If $Z_v < B[x, y]$, update $B[x, y] = Z_v$.
Track whether any pixel in the footprint was updated or if the footprint overlaps with any pixel that has a finite depth value.
**Refined Logic for Selection:** Before updating, check if the voxel's footprint is fully occluded.
*   **Additional Attributes:** Each voxel can store extra data specific to the application.
The in-memory structure requires storing the byte sequence and an offset array.
The rendering pass only processes visible voxels.
Reduced rendering time by avoiding computation for occluded voxels.
The culling pass adds an initial overhead, though it is offset by the reduced rendering work.
